name: Cable Station artificial surfing reef (Cables Reef, Cottesloe / Leighton, Perth, Western Australia)
status: DERIVED: every number in "global", "lines" and "extra_layers" is computed by the script from the published 3D-model data (no new measurement); the model inputs and their sources are in "key_inputs" and in the model METHODS_3D.md.
frame: x alongshore (+ toward SOUTH, bearing 170.3 deg T; x_model = -x_canonical); y offshore (+ toward WEST, bearing 260.3 deg T). The frame is the design-drawing frame rotated 9.74 deg ccw from true north: it is NOT shore-normal (fitted shoreline bearing 7.8 deg T, i.e. the y axis is about 17.5 deg off the shore normal).
datum: z = metres above MSL, MSL taken = AHD (A12). Surveyed versions are in AHD directly. Design versions: reading A (default for design) z_MSL = z_RL - 0.716 (Fremantle LWD to AHD, DNM TR12 Table 3, +-0.04 m); reading B: z_MSL = z_RL.
shoreline_definition: y = 0 is the NOMINAL origin line of the design frame (centroid of the original footprint at y = 271 m, Pattiaratchi 1999 / Blacka 2013), not the surveyed shoreline. The surveyed 0 m AHD line (fitted line, bearing 7.8 deg T) lies 254 m due east of the anchor (centroid) (shore_and_datum.py); y_true_shoreline is DERIVED from that (see derived_true_shoreline). The seabed grid starts at y = 190 m, so the MSL crossing is not in the model.
units: metres; offshore_m = model y (distance from the model shoreline y = 0, positive offshore); elevations in metres above MSL (z up); x = alongshore model axis

method.reef_surface: model.js versions[survey_surface_1999_11].grid.h_cm_b64 (int16 cm, z_MSL=AHD, 0.5 m cells, x already flipped to the model frame): rock thickness = DoT WA singlebeam soundings of 22 Nov 1999 (840 soundings, AHD) minus the measured 30 Mar 1998 pre-construction bed, linearly interpolated between sounding lines inside the original-plan footprint + 6 m, Gaussian-smoothed 1 m; footprint = the georeferenced Lyons (1992) original-plan outline (4,049 m2).
method.seabed: model.js seabed (5 m grid, y 190-420 m, x -150..150 m): DoT WA singlebeam of 30 Mar 1998 (pre-construction) inside the survey, Perth_5m composite elsewhere; AHD = MSL.

sampling.interpolation: seabed: bilinear on the model grid / analytic profile; reef surface: NaN-aware (normalised) bilinear on the reef grid; profiles at constant model x
sampling.footprint_rule: a reef cell belongs to the footprint if (reef surface - natural seabed) >= 0.10 m (ASSUMPTION, avoids zero-thickness tapers)
sampling.crest_line: x of the shallowest reef-surface cell
sampling.crest_zone: contiguous points on the line within 0.10 m of the line maximum (ASSUMPTION)
sampling.ramp: seaward ramp = from the seaward edge of the crest zone to the seaward end of the reef run (the toe); ramp_length = horizontal distance, ramp_rise = reef-surface drop over it, mean_seaward_slope = rise/length
sampling.max_seaward_slope: maximum over the ramp of (z[y-1 m] - z[y+1 m]) / 2 m (central difference, 2 m baseline), tan, degrees and 1:n
sampling.toe: seaward toe = most offshore point of the reef run (reef surface still >= 0.10 m above the seabed); the reef elevation, seabed elevation and thickness there are reported (thickness > 0.5 m means the model surface is cut at its outline, not at the seabed)
sampling.gap_bridging: gaps up to 12 m along a line are bridged when forming the reef run (ASSUMPTION; only Narrowneck is affected)
sampling.alongshore_length: span = x_max - x_min of footprint cells with reef surface >= level; union = number of x-columns containing such a cell * dx. Two levels are reported because "crest -0.5 m" is ambiguous: (a) z >= -0.5 m MSL and (b) z >= crest - 0.5 m
sampling.offshore_distance: offshore_m is measured from the model shoreline y = 0 (definition in shoreline_definition); offshore_from_msl_line_m uses the first downward crossing of z = 0 (MSL) of the modelled natural seabed on the same line

key_inputs.input: plan outline / design (Lyons 1992 design plan, Fig. A.2)

sources.B2013: Blacka, M.J., Shand, T.D., Carley, J.T. and Mariani, A. (2013) A Review of Artificial Reefs for Coastal Protection in NSW. WRL Technical Report 2012/08 (final, 11 June 2013), UNSW Water Research Laboratory, for the NSW Office of Environment and Heritage. https://doi.org/10.4225/53/58e1dc7368c7a (Fig. A.2 p.93 reproduces Lyons (1992) design plan; Table 4.3 p.67 tide range 0.8 m). Read in Lior's copy in papers/ (intake note 05_qa/papers_intake/P8_blacka_2013.md); cited per 07_scale/shapes/cables-reef-wa/3d/METHODS_3D.md reference 1.

key_inputs.input: Nov 1999 rock surface (840 soundings, AHD), 1998 pre-construction bed

sources.DoT_FR: Department of Transport, Western Australia, Coastal Information Branch (file dated 2020-11-11) Bathymetry point data, Fremantle (FR) package, FR.zip: FR19980330_Reef_Single.txt (30 Mar 1998), FR19991122_Single.txt (22 Nov 1999), FR20020201_Single.txt (1 Feb 2002); single-beam, GDA94 / MGA 50, m AHD; licence CC BY 4.0. https://s3-ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/transport.wa/Bathymetry/PointData/FR.zip ; catalogue https://catalogue.data.wa.gov.au/dataset/dot-bathy ; accessed 2026-10-10 (per cables-reef-wa/3d/METHODS_3D.md reference 9).

key_inputs.input: seabed outside the survey (Perth_5m, AHD) and shoreline (0 m AHD contour)

sources.DoT_5m: Department of Transport, Western Australia (file dated 2020-11-11) Composite surface Perth_5m.tif (WA Bathymetry, 5 m cells, AHD); licence CC BY 4.0. https://s3-ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/transport.wa/Bathymetry/Rasters/Perth_5m.tif ; dataset https://catalogue.data.wa.gov.au/dataset/composite-surfaces-index ; accessed 2026-10-10 (per cables-reef-wa/3d/METHODS_3D.md reference 10).

key_inputs.input: datum: AHD = MSL 1966-68 = 0.716 m above Fremantle gauge zero

sources.Roelse1975: Roelse, A., Granger, H.W. and Graham, J.W. (1975) The Adjustment of the Australian Levelling Survey 1970-1971. Division of National Mapping, Department of Minerals and Energy, Technical Report 12, 2nd edition, Canberra. Table 3 (Fremantle MSL 1966-68 = AHD 0.000 is 0.716 m above gauge zero). https://d28rz98at9flks.cloudfront.net/69874/Tech_Rep_DNM_012.pdf ; accessed 2026-10-13 (per cables-reef-wa/3d/METHODS_3D.md reference 13).

caveats: Default surface is a MEASURED single-beam survey (+-0.3 m, interpolated between ~5 m sounding lines, smoothed 1 m) of the month before completion (Nov 1999): crest top -1.55 m AHD, highest sounding -1.40 m. Feb 2002 survey: -1.71 / -1.67 m.
Footprint is the original design outline; the drawn south-arm extension is NOT confirmed (23 soundings).
Footprint edge cells keep a non-zero rock thickness (survey interpolation within the outline), so the surface does not taper to zero at the toe.
Design crest RL -1.0 = -1.72 m AHD (reading A) or -1.00 m (B); the surveyed surface is 0.13-0.22 m higher than reading A (physical/survey, not datum).

centreline.definition: cross-shore line (constant model x) at the alongshore mid-point of the reef footprint bounding box

crest_line.definition: cross-shore line (constant model x) through the shallowest crest cell of the reef surface (ties within 0.02 m: the cell nearest the middle of the shallowest plateau)

second_crest_line.definition: cross-shore line through the shallowest reef cell on the OTHER side of the centreline than the main crest line (for two-arm reefs: the other arm); crest cell z = -1.72 m MSL

reconstruction_check.what: volume of the reef grid read here (sum of max(reef - seabed, 0) over all finite reef cells, no thickness threshold, seabed from this script) against the volume stated by the model for the same version; a check that the surface was reconstructed as the viewer draws it

extra_layers.name: design_plan_original_1999 (datum reading A)
extra_layers.note: Design surface on the measured bed, original-plan footprint (Lyons 1992 / Blacka 2013 Fig. A.2), crest RL -1.0 = -1.72 m AHD (reading A, offset 0.716 m); grid versions[design_plan_original_1999].grid. Not the default; included because the surveyed default surface stops at the design outline with 1.5-2.6 m of rock still standing at the outer edge, so its seaward slopes are not toe-to-crest slopes.
